question: Which durable Dreaming scoping contract should OpenClaw accept for this issue: per-agent `agents.list[].dreaming`, a memory-core `dreaming.agents` allowlist, schedule/stagger/backoff controls, or a staged split?
rationale: The requested behavior adds user-facing config surface in a strict schema and there are now two open PRs with different API shapes; automation cannot safely choose the permanent product contract.

options.title: Adopt scoped allowlist first
options.body: Review https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/100057 as the first landing path, because it scopes Dreaming at the memory-core plugin boundary with proof and can leave per-agent schedules for a follow-up.

options.title: Use per-agent config
options.body: Continue with https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/67420 or a successor if maintainers want each agent entry to own `dreaming.enabled` and later schedule fields.

options.title: Pause new config surface
options.body: Keep the global sweep for now and focus on pressure/backoff work such as https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/84847 if another Dreaming config key is not desired.

recommendation.title: Adopt scoped allowlist first
recommendation.body: Review https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/100057 as the first landing path, because it scopes Dreaming at the memory-core plugin boundary with proof and can leave per-agent schedules for a follow-up.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent dreaming/config work and repository policy make this primarily a product/API direction call around memory-core configuration compatibility.
